title: Stone Village House in Erice
description: Two-stone buildings on terraced land in the medieval hilltop town of Erice, perched at 751m with sweeping views to the sea. Main 80 sqm residence plus an 85 sqm annex across two levels. Includes a swimming pool on the highest terrace. Town walls, Norman castle and cobblestone lanes are steps away. 15 min drive to Trapani train station.

title: Restored House in Palazzo Adriano
description: Completely restored three-level stone house in the medieval hilltop village of Palazzo Adriano (famous as the filming location for Cinema Paradiso). Spacious 135 sqm with living room, kitchen, kitchenette and bathroom on ground level, dining room and bedroom on first floor, large living room and second bedroom upstairs. Supermarket, bakery, café and pharmacy all within walking distance.

title: €1 House Program — Mussomeli
description: Italy's most internationally known €1 house program. The municipality of Mussomeli has sold 200+ homes to buyers from 30+ countries. Properties typically range from 50–150 sqm in the historic centre. A €5,000 refundable deposit is required; renovation must begin within 1 year. English-speaking estate agents operate locally. Population: 11,000 — good services, cafés, shops, pharmacy.

title: €1 House + €25K Grants — Troina
description: One of Italy's most generous €1 schemes. Troina sits at 1,121m — the highest elevation €1 town in Sicily, dramatically reducing tsunami risk. ~30 properties immediately available; 100+ more coming. Bonus: up to €15,000 restyle grant + €10,000 energy efficiency grant (€25K total support). Municipal agency House Troina provides full English-language assistance, including contractor referrals. Sicily's historic 'Greek-Byzantine' town.

title: €1 House — Gangi, Most Beautiful Village
description: Gangi is one of Italy's 'Most Beautiful Villages' (Borghi più belli d'Italia) and sits at over 1,000 meters, offering spectacular views across the Madonie mountains. Over 100 homes have already been sold through the programme. The village retains its medieval streetplan, Norman-Arab castle and 14th-century church. Cool summers due to altitude. 80km from Palermo airport.

title: €3 House — Sambuca di Sicilia (Zona Saracena)
description: Sambuca's Zona Saracena (Arab quarter) sells historic homes for just €3. One of the world's most famous €1 schemes with 250+ homes sold, CNN coverage, and a thriving international community. €5,000 deposit; 3-year renovation window. 30 km inland from the coast, surrounded by vineyards and olive groves with views to Lake Arancio. 90 min from Palermo.

title: €1 House — Salemi Historic Centre
description: Salemi is Italy's pioneering €1 house town (programme started 2008) and historic first capital of a liberated Italy under Garibaldi. Sited 20km inland in the Belice Valley wine and olive oil country. Norman castle and Arab-influenced streets. 11km from Salemi-Gibellina train station. Close to Marsala, Segesta Greek temple and Sicily's finest white wine country.

title: €1 House — Caltagirone (UNESCO Heritage Town)
description: Caltagirone is a UNESCO World Heritage city renowned worldwide for its ceramic arts tradition and the spectacular 142-step Scala di Santa Maria del Monte staircase, each step tiled uniquely. Population 35,000 — the largest €1 town with excellent services, university, hospital and direct trains to Catania (30 min). €5,000 suretyship; 3-year safety-work requirement.

title: €1 House — Petralia Soprana (Madonie Mountains)
description: The highest village in the Madonie mountains at 1,147m, with panoramic views over Sicily and (on clear days) to the Aeolian Islands. Cool summers — a natural air conditioner. Medieval streetscape, 14th-century churches, Madonie Natural Park surroundings with ski resort nearby. Active €1 programme. 80km from Palermo.

title: €1 House — Castiglione di Sicilia (Etna Wine Country)
description: Nestled on the north slopes of Mount Etna in the prestigious Etna DOC wine zone. Medieval village with Norman castle, Byzantine frescoed churches, and lava-stone architecture. Tourism is growing rapidly here — Etna wine tourism, hiking, cycling. About 40km from Catania. The lava soil produces some of Italy's most sought-after Nerello Mascalese reds.

title: €1 House — Bivona (Valley of Temples Gateway)
description: Inland hilltop town at 650m in the Agrigento province, gateway to the Valley of the Temples UNESCO site. Active €1 programme. Surrounded by holm oak forests with an annual truffle festival. Peach orchards and vineyards. About 60km from Agrigento city and airport connections.

title: €1 House — Leonforte (Baroque Fountain Town)
description: Known for its famous 24-spout Baroque fountain (la Granfonte), the peach-farming heartland, and a charming historic centre. Central Sicily location near Enna, the highest provincial capital in Italy. Qualifying municipality for the 7% flat tax regime. 30km from Enna station.

title: €1 House — Calatafimi Segesta (Greek Temple Views)
description: Home town of the Segesta Greek temple (c. 420 BC), one of the best-preserved Doric temples in the world. Historic village where Garibaldi won the pivotal Battle of Calatafimi in 1860. Only 12km from the A29 motorway and Segesta train station. The Greek theatre, surrounded by hills, hosts summer opera performances.

title: Apartment in Noto (Baroque UNESCO City)
description: Apartment in Noto, the 'Capital of Baroque' and UNESCO World Heritage city, rebuilt entirely in ornate Baroque style after the 1693 earthquake. Easy walking distance to Noto's famous cathedral and corso. 30min drive to Syracuse, 90min to Catania airport. Near the stunning Vendicari nature reserve beaches.

title: €1 House — Corleone (Historic Mountain Town)
description: Yes, that Corleone — but today a peaceful agricultural town at 542m with a fascinating anti-mafia museum (CIDMA), medieval castle ruins, and sweeping countryside views. The town is actively reinventing itself via tourism and the €1 house programme. 60km south of Palermo. Good food, genuine community feel.

title: €1 House — Ollolai (Zero Earthquake Risk, Sardinia)
description: Sardinia is Italy's ONLY seismically inactive region (Zone 4) — the safest in all of Italy. Ollolai's €1 programme includes the innovative 'Work from Ollolai' initiative that specifically targets remote workers and digital nomads. Mountain village at ~900m in the Barbagia heartland. Stone houses, traditional costume festivals, ancient nuraghe towers nearby. 3.5 hrs drive from Cagliari airport.

title: €1 House — Nulvi (Sassari Province, Sardinia)
description: Small Sardinian village with 4 properties immediately available through the €1 scheme. The town council actively recruits creatives, remote workers and international families. 2 hours drive from Sassari city (hospital, airport connections). Zone 4 seismicity — completely earthquake-free. Nuragic towers and cork oak forests within walking distance.

title: €1 House — Bonnanaro (Northwest Sardinia)
description: Interior village in the Logudoro area of northwest Sardinia, known for Romanesque churches, traditional textiles and olive oil production. Zone 4 — geologically the most stable area in Italy. 45km from Sassari. Qualifying municipality for Italy's 7% flat tax regime. Mild climate year-round. Less visited by tourists — authentic Sardinian living.

title: €1 House — Montresta (Oristano, Sardinia)
description: Tiny hilltop hamlet in the Marghine uplands of central-west Sardinia. Active €1 programme. Zone 4 seismicity. The crystal-clear waters of Bosa and the Cape Marargiu coast are 30km away. Bosa — arguably Sardinia's most colourful river town — is a 35-min drive. Extremely remote; best for those seeking complete tranquillity.

title: €1 House — Romana (Sassari, Sardinia)
description: Small village in Sassari province with active €1 scheme. Gentle rolling hills, cork oak forest, clear streams. Under 1 hour from Sassari city (airport, university hospital, trains to Cagliari). Zone 4 — completely earthquake-free. Qualifying municipality for Italy's preferential 7% flat tax on foreign income.

title: Stone House in Castiglione Messer Marino
description: Medieval village stone house at 1,000m in the Maiella highlands. Main stone residence (3 levels, ~45 sqm/floor) with living room + fireplace, two bedrooms, valley views, and wood-burning oven in basement. Separate 110 sqm outbuilding for renovation. Ski resorts 40 min away, Trabocchi Coast beaches 75 min away, Pescara Airport 90 min. Population: 1,575.

title: Habitable House in Castel del Monte (Gran Sasso Park)
description: Completely restored autonomous house at 1,350m in one of Italy's most beautiful medieval hamlets, inside Gran Sasso e Monti della Laga National Park. Three levels with kitchen, dining room with stove, two bedrooms (one with terrace), cellar and courtyard. One of Italy's 'Borghi più belli'. 1.5 hrs from Rome Fiumicino. Famous for Canestrato di Castel del Monte Slow Food pecorino cheese.

title: Move-in Ready Townhouse in Colledimezzo
description: Ready to move into — no renovation required. Three-floor townhouse with master bedroom + panoramic terrace, second bedroom, fully equipped kitchen with views, living room, full bathroom with bathtub, and 35 sqm cellar with separate entrance. Central heating, all utilities connected. 38km to the Adriatic coast, 85km to Pescara Airport, 46km to ski resort. Managed by Abruzzo Rural Property.

title: Farmhouse in Civitella Casanova (Pescara Hinterland)
description: Substantial farmhouse of 200 sqm with 12 hectares of agricultural land in the hilly Pescara hinterland. Commanding hilltop position with views to the Gran Sasso massif. 45 min to Pescara airport (international flights to UK/Germany/Netherlands). 30 min to the Adriatic coast. Excellent Airbnb potential: walking, cycling, truffle hunting in the hills.

title: €1 House — Pratola Peligna (No Deposit Required)
description: Italy's most buyer-friendly €1 scheme: NO security deposit required (unique among all Italian €1 programmes). 630 degraded buildings identified; ~250 eligible for the programme. Penalty €10,000 if no renovation plan submitted within 6 months (only if you don't act, not an upfront cost). In the Peligna Valley near L'Aquila — rebuilt post-2009 earthquake with modern infrastructure. L'Aquila hospital 1.5 hrs.

title: House in Ofena (Gran Sasso Foothills)
description: Stone house in a small village on the Gran Sasso foothills, in one of central Italy's warmest microclimates. 'Ofena cauldron' is famous for its sheltered warmth even in winter. Medieval tower, saffron fields (Abruzzo DOP saffron), dramatic limestone cliffs nearby. L'Aquila 45 min; Pescara 1hr.

title: Farmhouse in Agnone (Alta Molise, 350 sqm)
description: Enormous farmhouse of 350 sqm with 15+ rooms and 1,500 sqm of private land, just 1.5km from Agnone town centre. Three floors, double driveway. Agnone is known as the 'Athens of Samnium' — home to the world's oldest bell foundry (Marinelli, since 1339), still making bells for the Vatican. Hospital 2.4 km. Alta Molise mountains, rivers and trails surround the town.

title: €1 House — Castropignano (Molise Medieval Village)
description: Molise is Italy's second-smallest and least-visited region — a hidden gem. Castropignano has a spectacular Aragonese castle perched dramatically on a rock spur. Active €1 scheme. Qualifying municipality for the Molise €27,000 relocation grant (€700-900/month for 3 years). Combined with €1 house this is one of Italy's best-value packages. 1hr from Campobasso (train to Naples).

title: Detached House in Colletorto (Molise)
description: Semi-detached house in the hilltop village of Colletorto, one of Molise's most photogenic towns with a distinctive historic skyline. Move-in ready with 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms. Panoramic terrace views over the Molise countryside. 1 hour from Termoli on the Adriatic coast. Campobasso (trains, hospital) 40km away.

title: Apartment in Lesina Lake (Puglia, Gargano)
description: Three-bedroom apartment on the shores of Lesina lagoon, a coastal lake separated from the Adriatic by a narrow sandbar in the Gargano national park. The lagoon is famous for its migratory birds and the celebrated Lesina eel. Near the Foresta Umbra beech forest and Gargano's dramatic white cliffs. Note: low elevation — consider flood risk.

title: €1-€13K Pre-Renovated Homes — Biccari
description: Italy's most flexible €1 scheme — Biccari maintains an online catalogue with properties ranging from €1 to €30,000, including pre-renovated homes typically priced €7,500–€13,000. Only a €3,000 deposit required; 3-year renovation window. The municipality has invested €650K+ and established a dedicated real estate agency with legal and technical experts. 640m elevation, sub-Apennine setting with Lago di Occhito reservoir below.

title: €1 House — Candela (Tavoliere Plains, Puglia)
description: Small town of 2,700 inhabitants elevated at 500m above the Tavoliere plains. Active €1 house programme. Panoramic views of the Apennines and Adriatic. Nearby Saraceno Lake (reservoir) for water sports. 45 min from Foggia (high-speed trains to Naples, Rome). The area is known for the Candela sulphur springs.

title: Detached House in Ceglie Messapica (Itria Valley)
description: Stone house in Ceglie Messapica, the 'culinary capital of Puglia' in the Itria Valley among trulli and olive groves. The town is famous for its biscottini di Ceglie, local trattorias and white limestone streets. Near Ostuni (the white city), Alberobello trulli (UNESCO), and the Adriatic coast beaches.

title: €1 House — Caprarica di Lecce (Salento)
description: Small village 15km from Lecce, the 'Florence of the South' with its spectacular Baroque architecture, and 40km from Otranto's Adriatic beaches. Active €1 programme in the heart of Salento — olive oil, folk music (pizzica), and some of Italy's bluest sea. Direct trains from Lecce to Bari (high-speed to Rome).

title: €1 House — Zungoli (Medieval Hill Town, Campania)
description: One of the 'Most Beautiful Villages of Italy'. Zungoli is a striking medieval stone hill town with its distinctive gradoni (stone steps/streets), Aragonese castle and panoramic Irpinia valley views. Round 4 of the €1 scheme launched in 2024. Only €2,000 refundable deposit (lowest in Italy). 60km from Avellino city, 90min from Naples airport. Nearby Irpinia wines (Taurasi DOCG).

title: €1 House — Pietramelara (Near Naples, Campania)
description: Received 200 applications within 6 months of its 2021 launch — testament to its appeal. Only 50km from Naples, near the Royal Palace of Caserta (UNESCO). Caserta train station gives direct access to Naples (30 min) and Rome high-speed (1.5 hrs). Matese mountains and Caserta Vecchia medieval town nearby. Good all-round access to southern Italy's culture and coast.

title: €1 House — Bisaccia (Irpinia, Campania)
description: Elevated Irpinia mountain village at 750m with a 10th-century castle, baroque churches and sweeping views of the Apennines. Active €1 programme. Qualifying municipality for the 7% flat tax. Known for its high-quality olive oil and Lacryma Christi wines from nearby Vesuvian slopes. 1.5 hrs from Naples.

title: €1 House — Teora (Campania, Post-Earthquake Revival)
description: Small mountain village that was partially destroyed in the 1980 Irpinia earthquake and extensively rebuilt. Modern infrastructure alongside historic stone streets. Active €1 programme to repopulate the historic centre. 716m elevation. Known for wild chestnuts and local salumi. About 90 min from Salerno (high-speed trains to Rome and Naples).

title: €1 House — Acerenza (Basilicata, Cathedral Village)
description: One of Italy's most dramatic hilltop villages at 833m, dominated by its 11th-century Norman Romanesque cathedral — one of southern Italy's finest. Active €1 programme. 7% flat tax qualifying municipality. 30km from Potenza (trains connecting south to Taranto and north to Naples). Basilicata is increasingly called 'The New Tuscany' by Italian lifestyle media.

title: Top-to-Bottom House in Amelia (Umbria, Historic Walled City)
description: Spacious 5-bedroom, 150 sqm house inside Amelia's extraordinary Cyclopean stone walls (300 BC polygonal masonry), one of Italy's least-known historic walled cities. Amelia is a superb base for exploring Umbria — 40min from Orvieto, 1hr from Rome, 1hr from Assisi. Orvieto train station connects to Rome (1hr) and Florence (2hr). Excellent all-round location.

title: House in Massa Martana (Umbrian Hill Village)
description: Historic stone house in a small medieval village between Spoleto and Todi. Upper Umbria is renowned for its truffles, olive oil and wine. The Umbrian railway connects to Rome (2hrs), Florence (2hrs) and Assisi (1hr). Zone 2 seismic — Umbria's 1997 earthquake was significant but buildings are now extensively retrofitted.

title: Stone House in Bagnone (Lunigiana, Tuscany)
description: Semi-detached stone house in Bagnone, a Lunigiana borghe village in northern Tuscany. Zone 3 (low seismic risk). Lunigiana is Tuscany's most overlooked province — medieval castles, chestnut forests, crystal rivers and virtually no mass tourism. 1hr from the Cinque Terre coast, 1.5hrs from Pisa airport, 1hr from La Spezia (TGV to Paris).

title: Townhouse in Cingoli (Marche, Balcony of the Marches)
description: Cingoli is called 'the balcony of the Marches' for its 360° panoramic position at 631m, with views stretching from the Apennines to the Adriatic. Three-bedroom semi-detached house, 119 sqm, move-in ready. 40km from Ancona (international airport, Adriatic ferries to Croatia/Greece). 1.5hrs from Rimini. A relatively unknown gem of central Italy.

title: Apartment in Valbondione (Bergamo Alps, Near Lake)
description: Mountain apartment at 1,020m in the Bergamo Alps, head of the Seriana Valley and gateway to the Orobie natural park. Zone 3 (low seismic risk). Near Lake Iseo. 1hr from Bergamo (Ryanair hub; direct flights UK, Spain, etc.). 1hr from Milan (high-speed to Paris, Geneva, Zurich). Spectacular skiing and hiking. Authentic northern Italian mountain culture.

title: Villa in Locatello (Bergamo Alps, Lake Iseo Region)
description: Three-bedroom villa at 650m in Bergamo's pre-Alpine hills, in the Imagna Valley. Zone 3 (low seismic risk). 30km from Bergamo city and airport. Close to Lake Iseo and Lake Como. Northern Italian mountain village character — stone houses, cobbled lanes, genuine community. Strong Airbnb potential for walking and cycling tourism. 1hr from Milan.

title: Terraced House in Boccioleto (Vercelli Alps)
description: Alpine village house at 790m in the Valsesia valley, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Zone 3 (low seismic risk). Famous for Monte Rosa mountaineering and the Walser cultural heritage. 1.5hrs from Milan. Near Varallo Sacro Monte (UNESCO) — one of Italy's most spectacular religious hilltop sanctuaries. Clean mountain air, ancient stone houses and roaring streams.

title: Semi-detached House in Calliano (Monferrato Wine Hills)
description: Enormous 350 sqm, 5-bedroom property in the UNESCO Monferrato wine hills — heart of Barbera d'Asti and Grignolino territory. Zone 3 (low seismic risk). 15min from Asti (trains to Turin 1hr, Milan 1.5hrs). Surrounded by rolling vineyard hills, medieval castles and villages. Exceptional Airbnb potential for wine tourism — growing market in Piedmont's UNESCO wine landscape.

title: House in Noasca (Gran Paradiso National Park)
description: Mountain stone house at 1,060m inside Italy's oldest national park — Gran Paradiso. Zone 3 (low seismic risk). Crystal rivers, ibex, chamois and eagles are your neighbours. 1hr from Turin (TGV to Paris, Milan, Zurich). Excellent hiking and ski tourism base. Aosta Valley and Courmayeur (ski resort, Mont Blanc) are 1.5hrs away.

title: Farmhouse in Ceva (Piedmont, Langhe Gateway)
description: Large 350 sqm farmhouse on the edge of the Langhe and Ligurian Apennines — gateway between the UNESCO Langhe wine hills (Barolo, Barbaresco) and the Ligurian coast (1hr). Zone 3 (low seismic risk). Ceva has a train station with connections to Turin (1.5hrs) and Savona on the Riviera (1hr). Extraordinary potential for wine/truffle tourism Airbnb.

title: House in Castelli (Abruzzo, Majolica Ceramics Village)
description: Move-in ready house in Castelli, world-famous since the 12th century for its majolica ceramics tradition — every building in the village is decorated with hand-painted tiles. 3 bedrooms, 1 bathroom, 108 sqm. Near Gran Sasso and Laga Mountains National Park. 1hr from Pescara airport (European connections). Village has a state ceramics school — unique artisan atmosphere.
